(`claude mcp list` returned "No MCP servers configured.") I won't fall back to fetching the pages over HTTP and calling that an assessment. That would be a different kind of evidence presented as if it were a real browser run.

Before you re-run, two parts of the request won't go the way you described:

- **The ICP check doesn't use outside research.** It only uses what the run records on Nimbus Notes itself. That means the website visit, the signed-in product, or both. Every attribute in a profile has to point to a screenshot or log line from that capture. G2 and Capterra reviews, competitors' targeting and market-size figures aren't part of it. If I mixed them in, the profiles would look evidence-backed when part of them isn't. Anything the run can't show, the report lists as unknown instead of guessing. You can do that desk research separately and set it beside the three profiles. For a real side-by-side against named competitors, `/understudy:compare` runs the same checks on each site.
- **The interview can't be skipped.** The URL answers one of about nine questions. The others still need your answers, one at a time:
  - whether to assess the website, the signed-in product, or both
  - what the stand-in visitors should be trying to do
  - which devices to use
  - time limits
  - where the output goes and in what format

It takes a few minutes, and the answers decide what the run spends hours doing.

Once Playwright is connected and Claude Code is restarted, run `/understudy:run https://example-nimbus-notes.test` and I'll start the interview with ICP set as the objective. The session model is Opus 5.5, so you don't need to switch models.
